options: only citizens must obey the law
everyone, including officials, must obey the law
the law applies only in courts
q.explanation: The rule of law applies to everyone, and officials must observe the limits on their power.

q.q: Pick the option that lists the three branches of government named in the lesson, in the order given there.
q.explanation: The lesson names the legislative, executive and judiciary organs for the purpose of check and balance.

q.q: Explain why constitutionalism is described as being beyond having a constitution.
q.answer: real implementation of the principles is required|a constitution alone is not enough|the government must actually obey the supreme law
q.explanation: Constitutionalism is all about the real implementation of the fundamental constitutional principles, not just the document.

q.q: Which was the first written constitution of Ethiopia?
q.explanation: The first written constitution was introduced in 1931 by Emperor Haile Selassie I.

q.q: Ethiopia used traditional or unwritten constitutions until 1931.
q.explanation: Ethiopia used traditional or unwritten constitutions until the first written constitution in 1931.

q.q: The traditional document that justifies that Ethiopian monarchs derived their power to rule from God is:
q.explanation: Kibre Negest, or Glory of Kings, justifies that the monarchs derived their power from God.

q.q: The first written constitution was granted to the people by Emperor ____.
q.answer: Haile Selassie I|Haile Selassie|Haileselassie
q.explanation: Emperor Haile Selassie I granted the first written constitution in 1931.

q.q: The period from 1974 to 1987 in Ethiopian political history is known as:
q.explanation: The period from 1974 to 1987 is known as a constitutional vacuum or lacuna.

q.q: Which Ethiopian constitution introduced secularism, the separation of state and religion, for the first time?
q.answer: the 1987 PDRE constitution|1987 constitution|PDRE|1987
q.explanation: The 1987 PDRE constitution introduced secularism for the first time in Ethiopia.

q.q: The 1995 FDRE constitution introduced for the first time:
q.explanation: The 1995 FDRE constitution introduced a federal state structure for the first time.

q.q: Ethiopia has a long history of constitutionalism along with its long constitutional experience.
q.explanation: Although Ethiopia has long constitutional experience, it does not have a good history and culture of constitutionalism.

q.q: Arrange these Ethiopian constitutional milestones in the correct chronological order, starting with the earliest.
q.explanation: The order is 1931, 1987, 1991 Transitional Charter, then 1995 FDRE constitution, so the earliest is the 1931 written constitution.

q.q: Give two fundamental constitutional principles of the 1995 FDRE constitution.
q.answer: popular sovereignty|supremacy of the constitution|respecting human and democratic rights|secularism|transparency and accountability
q.explanation: The principles are popular sovereignty, supremacy of the constitution, respect for human and democratic rights, secularism, and transparency and accountability.

q.q: The 1955 revised constitution had:
q.explanation: The 1955 revised constitution had 8 chapters and 131 articles.

q.q: Indigenous knowledge is best defined as knowledge that is:
options: developed by a local people through long social life and interaction with their environment
q.explanation: This is the textbook definition of indigenous knowledge.

q.q: Indigenous knowledge is the same in every society.
q.explanation: Because it rests on culture and traditions, indigenous knowledge differs from society to society.

q.q: Which of the following is NOT listed as an area of Ethiopia's rich indigenous knowledge?
q.explanation: The textbook lists architecture, pottery, medicine, agriculture, cottage industry, conflict resolution and environmental conservation.

q.q: Name the approach local elders use when they settle a conflict between a husband and wife.
q.answer: win-win|win win approach
q.explanation: Elders resolve the disagreement through a win-win approach.

q.q: Give the term for locally organised mechanisms that work according to the custom and norms of a given society to resolve disputes.
q.answer: indigenous conflict resolution
q.explanation: This is the glossary definition of indigenous conflict resolution.

q.q: Ethiopia is described in the lesson as a country with:
q.explanation: The lesson states that Ethiopia is a country with rich indigenous knowledge systems.

q.q: Indigenous knowledge is usually transmitted from elders to young people through practice, proverbs and stories.
q.explanation: Young people inherit the tradition from elders because they are tomorrow's elders.

q.q: According to the lesson, when a husband and wife get into conflict in most parts of Ethiopia they:
options: go directly to the woreda court
take the case to local elders first
ask the police to arrest one party
q.explanation: They take their case to local elders to resolve the disagreement through a win-win approach.

q.q: Explain in one sentence why indigenous knowledge differs from one society to another.
q.answer: it is based on that society's culture, traditions, rituals, values and beliefs|because cultures and environments differ
q.explanation: Indigenous knowledge grows from the particular culture and environment of a community, so it varies.

q.q: Give the name of one artisan craft listed among Ethiopia's indigenous technologies.
q.answer: pottery|weaving|iron smithing|jewelry|wood carving|leather work
q.explanation: Pottery, weaving, iron smithing, jewelry, wood carving and leather work are all listed.

q.q: Arrange the following in the order in which a local conflict is normally handled in an Ethiopian community.
options: An elder mediates between the parties
The two parties reach a win-win agreement
q.explanation: The disagreement comes first, then elder mediation, then a win-win agreement; a court case is the least usual step.

q.q: A responsible citizen is best described as a person who:
options: has knowledge and commitment to improve livelihood, community and country
q.explanation: This is the textbook definition of a responsible citizen.

q.q: Which is the indigenous conflict resolution mechanism of the Oromo people?
q.explanation: Jaarsummaa is practised by the Oromo; Guurt is Somali, Yejoka Gurage and Mada'a Afar.

q.q: In Ethiopia, indigenous conflict resolution mechanisms have paramount significance compared with modern courts in ensuring sustainable peace.
q.explanation: The lesson states that indigenous mechanisms are of paramount significance in ensuring sustainable peace.

q.q: Name the indigenous mechanism of the Somali people mentioned in the lesson.
q.answer: guurt|guurt system
q.explanation: The Guurt system is the Somali indigenous conflict resolution mechanism.

q.q: Indigenous technologies help Ethiopian citizens mainly because they:
options: use local products at reasonable cost with better accessibility
q.explanation: Local products are cheaper and more accessible than pricey and scarce imported products.

q.q: Young people have no part in indigenous conflict resolution because it belongs to elders only.
q.explanation: Young people inherit the tradition from elders because they are tomorrow's elders.

q.q: Give the term for the wise use of resources available in the natural environment.
q.answer: environmental conservation
q.explanation: This is the definition of environmental conservation given in the lesson.

q.q: Name the two Ethiopian communities given as examples of indigenous environmental conservation.
q.answer: konso and gedeo|gedeo and konso
q.explanation: Konso terracing and Gedeo agroforestry are the two examples.

q.q: Which of the following is a major indigenous technology in Ethiopia?
q.explanation: Wood carving, with pottery, weaving, iron smithing, jewelry and leather work, is a major indigenous technology.

q.q: State one attribute of responsible citizens shown by people who keep indigenous crafts alive despite negative attitudes.
q.answer: hard work|determination|respect for indigenous wisdom|valuing their own wisdom
q.explanation: Their dedication shows determination, hard work and respect for indigenous wisdom.

q.q: Arrange the following steps in the order in which a community dispute is peacefully settled by elders.
options: A peaceful settlement is agreed by both sides
The parties agree to bring the dispute to elders
Elders listen to both sides and apply local custom
A quarrel breaks out between two families
q.explanation: The quarrel comes first, then agreement to involve elders, then mediation, then a peaceful settlement.

q.q: An indigenous social institution is best defined as an institution established:
options: locally by voluntary cooperation of community members on the basis of mutual trust
by a private company for profit
q.explanation: This is the definition given in the lesson and glossary.

q.q: Which institution is established primarily to provide mutual aid in burial matters?
q.explanation: Idir is established primarily to provide mutual aid in burial matters and other community concerns.

q.q: Iqub pays the pooled money to members through a lottery method.
q.explanation: Members agree on a fixed contribution and the money is paid to members by lottery.

q.q: Name the institution that is a culture of labour sharing during ploughing, weeding and harvesting.
q.answer: debo|jigie|debo or jigie|jigi
q.explanation: Debo or Jigie is the culture of helping each other in agricultural and building work.

q.q: The stick that symbolises women's rights in the Oromo society is called:
q.explanation: Siinqee is literally a stick, Ulee, symbolising a set of rights exercised by women.

q.q: Give the name of the institution that provides interest-free loans to members in addition to burial support.
q.answer: idir|iddir
q.explanation: Idir acts as a credit institution by providing members with loans without interest.

q.q: Indigenous social institutions are found only in rural areas of Ethiopia.
q.explanation: Idir, for example, is widely practised among both rural and urban peoples.

q.q: Which of the following is a service provided by Idir besides burial matters?
options: Helping members cope with the death of livestock
q.explanation: Idir helps members cope with sudden risks such as the death of livestock, fire, theft and health problems.

q.q: Explain the main purpose of Mahber or Senbete.
q.answer: to help each other in serious problems and enjoy and socialise together|mutual help and social gatherings
q.explanation: Members help each other in serious problems, enjoy together and discuss common interests.

q.q: In which Oromo system does Siinqee symbolise married women's participation in public life?
q.answer: gadaa|gadaa system
q.explanation: In the Oromo Gadaa system Siinqee represents married women's participation in political, economic, social, cultural and religious activities.

q.q: Arrange the steps of an Iqub meeting in the correct order.
options: The winner receives the pooled money
Members agree on the amount and the date
Members contribute their money on the set date
The winner is chosen by lottery
q.explanation: First the group agrees on the amount and date, then members contribute, then the winner is drawn by lottery, then the money is paid.

q.q: Which statement best defines culture?
options: Only the food and dress of a group
Shared language, beliefs, values, norms and behaviours passed between generations
q.explanation: Culture is the shared language, beliefs, values, norms, behaviours and material objects passed from generation to generation.

q.q: There is no society without culture and cultural values.
q.explanation: The textbook states that there is no society without culture and cultural values that differentiate one society from others.

q.q: Culture is described as a lens because:
options: it is used to evaluate what is proper or improper
q.explanation: We evaluate what is proper or improper, normal or abnormal using our culture.

q.q: Name one element of culture mentioned in the lesson.
q.answer: language|beliefs|values|norms|rituals|customs|arts|music
q.explanation: Language, beliefs, values, norms, rituals, customs, arts and music are elements of culture.

q.q: Explain why cultural diversity is described as a source of beauty in Ethiopia.
q.answer: many cultures and practices give beauty|diversity gives beauty and attraction
q.explanation: Various peoples with varieties of cultures give beauty and attraction to our society.

q.q: Which behaviour shows respect for cultural diversity?
options: Judging other cultures by your own standards
Taking part respectfully in another community's ceremony
Refusing to learn about other cultures
q.explanation: Respect means recognising and appreciating practices that are not our own.

q.q: Learning about other cultures helps us avoid negative stereotypes and personal bias.
q.explanation: The lesson states that learning about cultures helps us recognise differences and avoid negative stereotypes and personal biases.

q.q: What do we call a fixed and oversimplified idea about a group of people?
q.answer: stereotype|negative stereotype
q.explanation: An oversimplified fixed idea about a group is a stereotype.

q.q: In the case study, a visitor joins an unfamiliar coffee ceremony respectfully. What value does she show?
q.answer: respect for cultural diversity|appreciation|tolerance
q.explanation: She accepts and appreciates a cultural practice that is not her own.

q.q: Arrange the steps for learning about another culture in the correct order.
q.explanation: The order is: notice, pause, ask, participate and appreciate.

q.q: Which is an example of cultural diversity in Ethiopia?
options: Coffee ceremonies differ across the country
There is a single uniform culture
q.explanation: Coffee drinking cultures and ceremonies differ across Ethiopia, showing cultural diversity.

q.q: Multiculturalism is best defined as:
options: A single culture for all citizens
A body of thought about how to respond to cultural and religious diversity
A law that bans local festivals
q.explanation: Multiculturalism is a body of thought about the proper way to respond to cultural and religious diversity.

q.q: In a multicultural society every culture is unique in itself.
q.explanation: In a multicultural society every culture is unique in itself and cultural uniformity is uncommon.

q.q: In today's Ethiopia multiculturalism has been adopted to:
options: reconcile the imbalance between upholding ethnic and national identity
q.explanation: It reconciles the imbalance between upholding ethnic and national identity by maintaining unity within diversity.

q.q: Give the strategy used to maintain and preserve a country's national unity out of diverse identities.
q.answer: multiculturalism
q.explanation: Multiculturalism is the best strategy to accommodate diversity and preserve national unity.

q.q: Multiculturalism weakens national unity.
q.explanation: Multiculturalism maintains unity within diversity; it does not weaken it.

q.q: Which two identities does multiculturalism in Ethiopia try to hold in balance?
q.answer: ethnic identity and national identity|ethnic and national identity
q.explanation: It balances ethnic identity with national identity.

q.q: Which statement about cultural uniformity is correct?
options: All multicultural societies have one culture
Cultural uniformity is uncommon in diversified societies
q.explanation: The lesson states that cultural uniformity is uncommon in diversified societies.

q.q: Explain why multiculturalism is described as the best strategy for diversity accommodation.
q.answer: maintains unity within diversity|accommodates diversity and preserves national unity
q.explanation: It accommodates diversity while maintaining and preserving national unity.

q.q: Arrange the way a state manages diversity.
q.explanation: The order is: recognise, accept, respect, balance and share values.

q.q: Which is an example of multiculturalism in Ethiopia?
options: Christians and Muslims living together peacefully for a long period
Forcing one dress style on all citizens
q.explanation: Christians and Muslims have lived together peacefully based on mutual respect and tolerance.

q.q: Which of the following is NOT a pillar of multicultural societies?
q.explanation: The four pillars are accepting, respecting, tolerating and appreciating differences, not ignoring them.

q.q: Tolerance is described as the bedrock of multiculturalism in diverse societies.
q.explanation: The lesson states that tolerance is the bedrock of multiculturalism in diverse societies like Ethiopia.

q.q: Tolerance is best defined as:
options: the willingness to accept the existence of differences we dislike or disagree with
refusing to meet people who differ
q.explanation: Tolerance is the willingness to accept the existence of differences we dislike or disagree with.

q.q: Give the pillar that means understanding how we are alike, how we are different and treating everyone with respect regardless of the differences.
q.answer: accepting differences|accepting difference
q.explanation: This is the definition of accepting differences.

q.q: Which pillar goes beyond tolerance by seeking to understand and learn about another culture?
q.answer: appreciating differences|appreciation
q.explanation: Appreciating differences seeks to understand and learn about another culture.

q.q: Respect should be given only to people whose culture is the same as ours.
q.explanation: We must respect and support each other despite differences in our cultural backgrounds.

q.q: Diversity encompasses which of the following?
options: Culture, gender, religion, age, disability and career status
q.explanation: Diversity encompasses culture, gender, religion, age, disability and career status.

q.q: Explain the difference between tolerance and appreciation of differences.
q.answer: tolerance accepts without approving|appreciation seeks to understand and value the difference
q.explanation: Tolerance accepts what we dislike, while appreciation positively values and seeks to understand the difference.

q.q: If differences are accepted and respected they help to create:
q.explanation: Accepted and respected differences create peaceful coexistence and harmonious relationships.

q.q: Arrange the four pillars from the most basic response to the fullest response.
q.explanation: The order is: accepting, respecting, tolerating and appreciating differences.

q.q: Which of the following is a major form of diversity demonstrating multiculturalism in Ethiopia?
q.explanation: Ethiopia shows ethnic, cultural, linguistic and religious diversity.

q.q: Ethnicity by itself is a potential threat to multiculturalism.
q.explanation: Ethnicity and identifying oneself is natural; it becomes a threat only when it develops into ethnocentrism.

q.q: The basis of ethnicity is often:
options: a tradition of common descent or intermarriage and shared culture or history
q.explanation: The basis of ethnicity is often a tradition of common descent or intermarriage and shared culture or history.

q.q: Give the term for judging other cultures as inferior by the standards of your own group.
q.answer: ethnocentrism
q.explanation: This is ethnocentrism, a potential threat to multiculturalism.

q.q: Name the principle that says different religions should live in harmony with each other.
q.answer: religious tolerance|tolerance
q.explanation: Religious tolerance dictates that different religions live in harmony.

q.q: Gender is best described as:
options: the socially constructed roles and relationships society ascribes to the two sexes
q.explanation: Gender is a social construct that defines roles, rights and responsibilities for women and men.

q.q: Disability is a fundamental aspect of human diversity.
q.explanation: The lesson states that disability is a fundamental aspect of human diversity in the present-day world.

q.q: Explain why embracing disability requires more than tolerance.
q.answer: it requires moving beyond tolerance to embracing and celebrating|practical accommodation and inclusion
q.explanation: Disability diversity moves beyond simple tolerance to embracing and celebrating each individual.

q.q: Linguistic diversity means:
options: the presence of a variety of languages spoken in a community
q.explanation: Linguistic diversity is the presence of a variety of languages spoken within a community.

q.q: Give one example from the lesson of religious groups living together peacefully in Ethiopia.
q.answer: Christians and Muslims|Christians and Muslims living together
q.explanation: Christians and Muslims have been living together peacefully based on mutual respect and tolerance.

q.q: Unity in diversity refers to:
options: the feeling of being one over common destinies among members of a group
the rule of one ethnic group
q.explanation: The lesson defines unity in diversity as the feeling of being one over common destinies among members of a group.

q.q: Unity in diversity means uniformity in all things.
q.explanation: Unity in diversity is not uniformity; it is harmony between dissimilar individuals or groups.

q.q: Which statement best describes unity in diversity?
options: Commonality without uniformity and diversity without fragmentation
q.explanation: The lesson states that unity in diversity involves commonality without uniformity and diversity without fragmentation.

q.q: What term means the feeling of oneness across the entire country?
q.answer: national unity
q.explanation: National unity is a feeling of oneness across the entire country.

q.q: Explain why unity in diversity is not the same as uniformity.
q.answer: unity respects differences|unity allows differences while keeping harmony|uniformity removes differences
q.explanation: Unity in diversity keeps differences and builds harmony, while uniformity removes differences.

q.q: Diversity means the existence of variations of different characteristics in a group of people.
q.explanation: Diversity refers to the existence of variations of different characteristics in a group.

q.q: Which of the following is NOT part of the meaning of unity in diversity?
options: Forcing everyone to be the same
q.explanation: Forcing sameness is uniformity, which is the opposite of unity in diversity.

q.q: Explain the difference between unity in diversity and national unity.
q.answer: national unity is oneness across the whole country|unity in diversity is harmony among dissimilar groups
q.explanation: National unity is oneness across the entire country, while unity in diversity is harmony among groups that differ.

q.q: Arrange these steps for upholding unity in diversity in the correct order.
options: Live together in harmony as one nation
Acknowledge the rich diversity in society
Design the right policy for diversity accommodation
q.explanation: The order is: acknowledge diversity, recognise and respect differences, design the right policy, then live in harmony.

q.q: Ethiopia is a country in which different peoples have lived together for many centuries. This shows:
q.explanation: Living together for many centuries shows the deep tolerance and unity of the Ethiopian people.

q.q: Unity in diversity is not about uniformity, but an expression of ____ between dissimilar groups.
q.answer: harmony
q.explanation: The lesson calls unity in diversity an expression of harmony between dissimilar individuals or groups.

q.q: Which of the following is NOT an element of diversity?
q.explanation: Language uniformity is the opposite of a diversity element; linguistic diversity is the correct element.

q.q: Cultural diversity refers to:
options: the occurrence of different cultures, religions, languages and ethnic backgrounds
q.explanation: Cultural diversity is the occurrence of different cultures, religions, languages and ethnic backgrounds.

q.q: In true cultural diversity, no culture is superior to another.
q.explanation: The lesson states that in true cultural diversity all cultures should be seen equally.

q.q: Religious diversity means that everyone follows the same religion.
q.explanation: Religious diversity is the fact that there are significant differences in religious beliefs and practices.

q.q: Name the diversity that refers to significant differences in religious beliefs and practices.
q.answer: religious diversity
q.explanation: Religious diversity is the fact of significant differences in religious beliefs and practices.

q.q: Explain what linguistic diversity is.
q.answer: the existence of different languages in a country|many languages in a country
q.explanation: Linguistic diversity is the existence of different languages in a given country.

q.q: Ethiopia is known as a land of peace and religious tolerance because:
options: Christians and Muslims and their places of worship live together peacefully
q.explanation: In Ethiopia churches and mosques are often in close proximity and relationships are peaceful, and indigenous beliefs also exist.

q.q: Give one advantage of respecting the equality of peoples from different backgrounds.
q.answer: peaceful coexistence|harmony|tolerance
q.explanation: Respecting equality helps people live in harmony and peace as citizens of one country.

q.q: Why does language matter in a diverse society?
options: It is one of the most important aspects of culture
It removes the need for respect
q.explanation: Language is one of the most important aspects of culture and can promote different cultural entities.

q.q: In cultural diversity, all cultures should be seen as ____.
q.answer: equal
q.explanation: All cultures should be seen equally, with none superior or inferior.

q.q: What would happen to tolerance and peaceful coexistence if Ethiopians did not respect cultural and religious diversity?
q.answer: tolerance would decrease|peaceful coexistence would be threatened
q.explanation: Without respect for diversity, tolerance would fall and peaceful coexistence would be at risk.

q.q: Accommodation of diversity is best described as:
options: a distinct strategy to deal with cultural diversity
q.explanation: Accommodation of diversity is the distinct strategy to deal with cultural diversity.

q.q: Diversity management is a process intended to:
options: create and maintain a positive environment where similarities and differences are valued
q.explanation: Diversity management creates and maintains a positive environment where similarities and differences are valued.

q.q: In accommodation of diversity, differences are accepted.
q.explanation: The lesson states that in accommodation of diversity differences are accepted.

q.q: Accommodation and integration mean exactly the same thing.
q.explanation: Integration aims at equal citizenship and the privatisation of differences, so it is distinct from accommodation.

q.q: According to the lesson, accommodation implies the right way to what?
q.answer: diversity management
q.explanation: Accommodation implies the right way to diversity management.

q.q: State when accommodation of diversity can be achieved.
q.answer: when the components of society accept differences and respect their consequences|mutual acceptance of differences
q.explanation: It is achieved when society's components demonstrate mutual acceptance of differences and respect their consequences.

q.q: Integration, as distinct from accommodation, aims at:
options: equal citizenship and the privatisation of differences
q.explanation: Integration aims at equal citizenship and at the privatisation of differences.

q.q: Explain why diversity accommodation ensures that everyone can participate fully.
q.answer: it removes barriers such as ability, religion or gender|it accepts differences and includes all
q.explanation: Diversity accommodation ensures that everyone, regardless of physical ability, religion or gender, is able to participate fully.

q.q: A workplace that values the similarities and differences of its employees is practising:
q.explanation: Diversity management creates a positive work environment where similarities and differences are valued.

q.q: Name one factor, besides religion and gender, that diversity accommodation takes into account.
q.answer: physical ability|disability
q.explanation: The lesson names physical ability, religion and gender as factors that should not prevent full participation.

q.q: Give one reason why diversity management is a prominent issue in developing countries like Ethiopia.
q.answer: multicultural societies need to accommodate diversity and achieve integration|many cultures live together
q.explanation: Managing cultural diversity has become prominent in developing countries such as Ethiopia, which must accommodate diversity and realise national integration.

q.q: Ethiopia contains how many ethnic groups according to the lesson?
q.explanation: Ethiopia contains over 80 different ethnic groups, each with tribes and sub-tribes.

q.q: Each ethnic group in Ethiopia has distinct cultural practices and speaks a language specific to the group.
q.explanation: The lesson states that each ethnic group has distinct cultural practices and speaks its own language.

q.q: Building unity in diversity from a multicultural state and a federal system has been adopted as a solution for:
q.explanation: It has been adopted as a solution for incorporating both unity and diversity.

q.q: A very crucial balance between unity and diversity within society is an easy goal to achieve.
q.explanation: The lesson states that this balance is not an easy goal to achieve.

q.q: A balance between unity and diversity is used to create national integration and a common national identity among all ____.
q.answer: nations|nations and nationalities
q.explanation: It is used to create integration and common identity among all nations.

q.q: List the differences that must be recognised and respected to ensure national unity and common identity.
q.answer: language, religion, identity, cultural values and historical background
q.explanation: The lesson names language, religion, identity, cultural values and historical background.

q.q: In the case study, the community welcomed Abdella warmly. This best shows:
options: respect for cultural and religious diversity
q.explanation: The community celebrated both Christian and Muslim holidays and respected religious diversity.

q.q: Explain how a sense of common citizenship is fostered among citizens of a state.
q.answer: when feelings of unity and harmony are in people's hearts|through shared unity and harmony
q.explanation: When feelings of unity and harmony are in the hearts of the peoples, a sense of common citizenship or loyalty to the nation is fostered.

q.q: Which factors does the lesson say must be considered to balance unity and diversity in Ethiopia?
q.explanation: The lesson stresses historical, political and socio-cultural factors.

q.q: According to the lesson, promoting diverse ethnic, linguistic, cultural and religious differences is as important as national unity.
q.explanation: The lesson states this equality of importance clearly.

q.q: What does the lesson call the process aimed at creating and maintaining a positive environment where similarities and differences are valued?
q.answer: diversity management
q.explanation: That is the definition of diversity management.

q.q: According to the lesson, a problem is:
options: an unpleasant situation that prevents people from achieving what they want
q.explanation: The textbook defines a problem as an unpleasant situation that prevents people from achieving what they want.

q.q: Problem-solving skills are described as valuable intellectual abilities for leading a successful life.
q.explanation: The lesson states that problem-solving skills are valuable intellectual abilities and capacities for leading a successful life.

q.q: Which statement best describes decision making?
options: Selecting the right option from a number of available alternatives
q.explanation: Decision making is about selecting the right option from available alternatives.

q.q: Give the term for the act of defining a problem, determining its cause, identifying and selecting alternatives, and implementing the solution.
q.answer: problem solving|problem-solving
q.explanation: This is the broader meaning of problem solving given in the lesson.

q.q: There is only one right way to solve any given problem.
q.explanation: The lesson says there is no right way to solve a given problem and different people solve it differently.

q.q: What is the step that must come before searching for a solution?
q.answer: define the problem|defining the problem
q.explanation: Defining and understanding the problem comes before finding the solution.

q.q: In the example of the lost bag, which skills does the lesson say the solution needs?
options: Creative problem solving and critical thinking
q.explanation: The lesson states that this serious problem needs creative problem solving and critical thinking skill.

q.q: Why is problem solving called a basic life skill?
options: Because it is taught only in Grade 9
Because it is needed at home, at school and at work every day
Because it applies only to engineers
Because it replaces all other skills
q.explanation: It is essential to our day-to-day lives at home, at school and at work.

q.q: Arrange the broad problem-solving process in the correct order.
options: Determine the cause of the problem
q.explanation: The order is: define the problem, determine the cause, identify and select alternatives, implement the solution.

q.q: Explain in one sentence how problem solving and decision making are linked.
q.answer: solving a problem involves making right decisions|they are inter-linked
q.explanation: The two are inter-linked because solving a problem tactfully involves making right decisions.

q.q: Where in daily life is the ability to solve problems said to be essential?
q.answer: home, school and work|at home and at school and at work
q.explanation: The lesson names home, school and work.

q.q: Problem-solving skills are considered to be:
options: a hard skill learned only at university
a soft skill, or an individual strength
a subject in the national timetable
q.explanation: The lesson describes problem solving as a soft skill rather than a learned hard skill.

q.q: Everybody may have problem-solving skill without formal education and training.
q.explanation: Because it is a soft skill, people may have it in different degrees without formal training.

q.q: Which of the following is listed as an importance of problem-solving skills?
q.explanation: Developing emotional intelligence is one of the listed benefits.

q.q: Name the method by which people settle differences and reach compromise while avoiding argument.
q.answer: negotiation|negotiation skill
q.explanation: This is the definition of negotiation skill.

q.q: Why does the lesson value indigenous problem-solving skills?
options: They are used to resolve social and individual problems in society
They are written in textbooks only
q.explanation: Indigenous skills include negotiation, cooperation and diversity tolerance used to resolve problems in society.

q.q: Indigenous skills should replace scientific skills in problem solving.
q.explanation: The lesson says integrating indigenous skills with scientific ones is very important.

q.q: Give the term for producing many facts, ideas and possible solutions before judging them.

altAnswers: Convert map scales and measure distance and area.
Locate places using grid references and compass bearings.
q.explanation: Taken directly from the MoE learning outcomes.

q.q: Explain in one sentence why interpreting maps and graphs matters.
q.answer: Interpreting Maps and Graphs is a core curriculum point tested in the national exam.
q.explanation: Any accurate statement linking the topic to the curriculum earns the mark.

q.q: Give a real-life example of interpreting maps and graphs in Ethiopia or the Horn of Africa.
q.answer: An Ethiopian example connected to interpreting maps and graphs, as discussed in the unit.
q.explanation: The exam rewards named local examples over generic ones.

q.q: The word history comes from the Greek word Istoria, which means:
q.explanation: Istoria means inquiry or an account of one's inquiries.

q.q: According to the textbook, history began about how many years ago?
q.explanation: History began about 5,500 years ago when people first began to write.

q.q: Prehistory is the time before people developed the art of writing.
q.explanation: Prehistory was the period before the art of writing was developed.

q.q: Every statement written in a history book is a historical fact.
q.explanation: Writers can mix opinions with facts; an opinion cannot be proved.

q.q: Name the people who study and write about the human past.
q.answer: historians
q.explanation: Historians are people who study and write about the human past.

q.q: Give the term for the study of the distant past, before writing was invented.
q.answer: prehistory
q.explanation: This is the definition of prehistory.

q.q: Which one best describes a historical fact?
options: A statement about the past that can be proved with supporting information
A story invented to entertain readers
q.explanation: A fact is a statement that can be proved with supporting information.

q.q: Which of these are primary needs that human beings produced by interacting with the natural environment?
q.explanation: People produced their primary needs, such as food, shelter and cloth, from nature.

q.q: Explain in one sentence why archaeologists and anthropologists are important for the study of prehistory.
q.answer: there are no written records|prehistory has no writing
q.explanation: Because prehistory left no written records, scholars must recover clues from material remains.

q.q: Arrange these steps in the order a historian follows to turn evidence into history.
options: Write an interpretation of what happened and why
Find and examine sources as evidence
Decide whether each source can be trusted
q.explanation: The historian first finds sources, then evaluates them, and finally writes an interpretation.

q.q: According to the lesson, history is a branch of which field?
q.explanation: History is a branch of social science that deals with what human beings did in the past.

q.q: History helps us know the past, understand the present and foresee future developments.
q.explanation: This is the importance of history stated in the textbook.

q.q: Who is often called the father of history?
q.explanation: The first use of the term is attributed to Herodotus (c. 484-425 BC).

q.q: Leopold Von Ranke (1795-1886) is considered the father of:
q.explanation: Ranke established history as an independent discipline and is called the father of modern historiography.

q.q: Give the term for sources that are contemporary with the events under study.
q.answer: primary sources|primary source
q.explanation: Primary sources are contemporary with the events they describe.

q.q: Give the name for the study of how knowledge of the past is attained and transmitted.
q.answer: historiography
q.explanation: This is the definition of historiography.

q.q: Which of the following is a secondary source?
options: A chronicle written at the time
A coin minted in the period
A letter written by a witness
q.explanation: A textbook derives its information from primary sources.

q.q: The Ethiopian calendar is:
options: exactly the same as the Gregorian calendar
seven to eight years behind the Gregorian calendar
ten years ahead of the Gregorian calendar
q.explanation: Ethiopia uses its own calendar, which is seven to eight years behind the Gregorian calendar.

q.q: The Islamic calendar counts time from the Hijra, the flight of the prophet Mohammed from Mecca to Medina in 622 AD.
q.explanation: The Hijra of 622 AD begins the Islamic calendar, with BH before it and AH after it.

q.q: Explain why the textbook says that where there are no sources there is no history.
q.answer: history is based on evidence from sources|without sources there is no evidence
q.explanation: History rests on evidence arising from sources, so no sources means no evidence and no history.

q.q: Arrange these steps in the order a historian follows when writing history.
options: Write an interpretation of what happened and why
Select a topic or problem to study
q.explanation: The historian selects a topic, collects and evaluates sources, then writes an interpretation.

q.q: All human beings living today belong to which species?
q.explanation: All human beings now living belong to the species Homo sapiens.

q.q: All hominids are characterised by bipedalism, that is walking on two feet in an upright position.
q.explanation: Bipedalism is a distinguishing feature of all hominids.

q.q: What name did Donald Johanson give to the fossil skeleton he found in Ethiopia in 1974?
q.answer: lucy|dinkinesh
q.explanation: He named his find Lucy, also known as Dinkinesh.

q.q: Homo erectus was the first hominid to:
options: leave Africa and move into Europe and Asia
q.explanation: Homo erectus were the first to leave Africa, using fire to keep warm in colder areas.

q.q: Which two major opposing theories explain the origin of human beings?
q.explanation: The two major opposing theories are the creationist and the evolutionist theories.

q.q: Give the term for the slow and natural process by which living things change from earlier forms.
q.answer: evolution
q.explanation: This slow and natural process is called evolution.

q.q: Who formulated the scientific theory of evolution?
q.explanation: The evolutionist theory was formulated by the English scientist Charles Darwin (1809-1882).

q.q: Explain why Ethiopia is important in the study of human evolution.
q.answer: fossils of hominids were found in ethiopia|remains of homo species were found in ethiopia|ethiopia and the horn have sites of all three homo species
q.explanation: Ethiopia has sites showing all three Homo sub-species in succession, along with the earliest hominid found at Aramis.

q.q: The earliest hominid found in Ethiopia was discovered at Aramis in the Middle Awash of the Afar region.
q.explanation: It was described by a team led by Tim White and dated to about 4.4 million years ago.

q.q: Name the genus to which Homo habilis, Homo erectus and Homo sapiens belong.
q.answer: homo
q.explanation: All three species belong to the genus Homo.

q.q: Arrange these hominids from the earliest to the latest.
q.explanation: The order is Australopithecus afarensis, Homo habilis, Homo erectus and Homo sapiens.

q.q: Which of these is one of the basic distinguishing features of the human species?
options: The ability to live in water
The ability to write from birth
q.explanation: One basic distinguishing feature of the human species is the ability to make tools.

q.q: The Paleolithic Age is also known as the:
q.explanation: Paleolithic is Greek for old stone, so it is the Old Stone Age.

q.q: The Neolithic Age started around 8,000 BC and lasted until about 4,000 BC.
q.explanation: These are the dates given for the Neolithic Age in the textbook.

q.q: During which period did human beings domesticate plants and animals?
q.explanation: Systematic agriculture and domestication belong to the Neolithic Age.

q.q: Give the term for the shift from hunting animals and gathering food to keeping animals and growing crops regularly.
q.answer: neolithic revolution|agricultural revolution|systematic agriculture
q.explanation: This shift is called the Neolithic Revolution or Agricultural Revolution.

q.q: Which tools appeared during the Neolithic Age?
options: The hoe, the yoke and the wheel
q.explanation: New and better tools such as the hoe, the yoke and the wheel appeared in the Neolithic Age.

q.q: The Mesolithic Age lasted from 9000 BC to 8000 BC.
q.explanation: The Mesolithic Age lasted from 9000 BC to 8000 BC.

q.q: Name one plant domesticated in Ethiopia during the Neolithic age.
q.answer: teff|dagussa|nug|enset
q.explanation: Teff, dagussa, nug and enset were among the domesticated plants.

q.q: Explain one major consequence of the Neolithic Revolution.
q.answer: sedentary way of life|people became food producers|complex social organisation|stone houses and granaries were built
q.explanation: The revolution produced settled life, food production and more complex society.

q.q: Which of these is a Neolithic archaeological site in Ethiopia?
q.explanation: Ethiopian Neolithic sites include Aksum, Lalibela, and places near Chercher in Hararghe and Metehara.

q.q: Arrange the three periods of the Stone Age from earliest to latest.
q.explanation: The order is Paleolithic, Mesolithic and Neolithic.

q.q: A state is best defined as:
options: a group of families living together
a politically organised body of people with a defined territory, a legitimate government and sovereignty
q.explanation: This is the definition of a state given in the textbook.

q.q: Which of the following is NOT one of the features a state must have?
q.explanation: The features listed are population, territory, government, sovereignty and recognition, not language.

q.q: For a state to exist it must have population, territory, government, sovereignty and recognition.
q.explanation: These five features are listed in the textbook.

q.q: Give the term for the early states that were ruled by priests.
q.answer: theocratic states|theocratic state
q.explanation: Early states ruled by priests were known as theocratic states.

q.q: According to the trade theory, who gradually replaced priests with the emergence of markets?
q.explanation: Village chiefs who controlled trade gradually replaced priests as markets emerged.

q.q: In the agricultural theory of the state, rich people who gained higher status because of their surplus are called:
q.explanation: Elites are rich people who attained higher status in society due to their wealth.

q.q: A state is exactly the same thing as a kingdom or an empire.
q.explanation: The textbook states clearly that a state differs from a kingdom and an empire.

q.q: According to one theory, villages combined to establish states under powerful local chiefs by what means?
q.answer: war|conflict|force
q.explanation: War or conflict could lead small villages to combine under powerful local chiefs by force.

q.q: Explain how agriculture is said to have led to the emergence of the state.
q.answer: surplus produced elites who gained control over others|society divided into higher and lower classes
q.explanation: Agricultural surplus created economic classes and wealthy elites, whose control over others led to the state.

q.q: The Neolithic way of life that preceded the state was based on:
q.explanation: The Neolithic age produced sedentary ways of life based on farming.

q.q: The civilization of ancient Egypt began at about:
q.explanation: The textbook states that the civilization of Ancient Egypt began at about 3000 BC.

q.q: Who, according to tradition, unified Upper and Lower Egypt?
q.explanation: According to tradition, Upper and Lower Egypt were unified by Menes around 3200 BC.

q.q: The viziers acted as mayors, tax collectors and judges.
q.explanation: The king ruled Egypt through officials named viziers, who acted as mayors, tax collectors and judges.

q.q: What is the name of the process of preserving a body, which helped Egyptians advance in medicine?
q.answer: mummification
q.explanation: The process of preserving the body is called mummification.

q.q: The Egyptian art of writing developed around 3000 BC is called:
q.explanation: Hieroglyphics was a combination of pictograms, ideograms, phonograms and determinatives.

q.q: Give the term for the paper-like substance that the ancient Egyptians introduced.
q.answer: papyrus
q.explanation: The Egyptians introduced papyrus, a paper-like substance.

q.q: Meroe was important mainly because of its flourishing iron industry.
q.explanation: Meroe was a centre of metal products such as gold, copper, silver and iron, indicating a flourishing iron industry.

q.q: The kingdom of Kush lasted until about 350 AD, when it was destroyed by:
q.explanation: At about 350 AD, the Aksumite king Ezana invaded and destroyed Meroe.

q.q: Explain why the Nile was central to the Egyptian economy.
q.answer: silt replenished the soil|farming and trade depended on the Nile
q.explanation: Silt from the Nile replenished the fertility of the soil, allowing large crops, and trade also used the river.

q.q: Arrange these events in correct chronological order from earliest to latest.
options: Kush first exists along the Nile
q.explanation: The order is: Menes unifies Egypt (c. 3200 BC), Kush exists (c. 2000 BC), the Kushites conquer Egypt (8th century BC), Ezana destroys Meroe (c. 350 AD).

q.q: Name one crop produced by the Egyptian peasantry.
q.answer: wheat|barley
q.explanation: The Egyptian peasantry produced wheat and barley.

q.q: The earliest great river valley civilization was found between which two rivers?
q.explanation: The Sumerian civilization was found between the rivers Tigris and Euphrates.

q.q: The large Sumerian stepped temple towers built of sun-dried mud bricks were called:
q.explanation: Large temples of this kind were called ziggurats, or stepped towers.

q.q: Cuneiform was a simple alphabet system.
q.explanation: Cuneiform was not an alphabet system; it was a highly complex system of ideographs.

q.q: Who founded the first Persian Empire around 550 BC?
q.answer: Cyrus the Great|Cyrus
q.explanation: The first Persian Empire was founded by Cyrus the Great around 550 BC.

q.q: Name the Persian religion founded by a prophet called Zoroaster.
q.answer: Zoroastrianism
q.explanation: Their religion was known as Zoroastrianism, founded by a prophet called Zoroaster.

q.q: The first Indian civilization began in the Indus Valley at about:
q.explanation: The first Indian civilization began in the Indus Valley at about 2500 BC and reached its apex at about 1500 BC.

q.q: Buddhism emerged from Hinduism as a reform movement and spread outside India.
q.explanation: Buddhism emerged from Hinduism as a reform movement and spread to South East Asia, China and Japan.

q.q: The first dynasty in China (c. 1700-1122 BC) was the:
q.explanation: The first dynasty in China was the Shang dynasty (c. 1700-1122 BC).

q.q: Explain why the Chinese constructed the Great Wall of China.
q.answer: to keep out invaders from central Asia|defence against invaders
q.explanation: The Great Wall was built to keep out invaders from central Asia.

q.q: Name the philosopher (551-479 BC) whose teaching is known as Confucianism.
q.answer: Confucius
q.explanation: Confucius (551-479 BC) was the most influential philosopher in Chinese history; his teaching was Confucianism.

q.q: Arrange these Asian civilizations or states from earliest to latest foundation.
q.explanation: Order: Sumerian cuneiform c. 3200 BC, Indus Valley c. 2500 BC, Shang dynasty c. 1700 BC, Persian Empire c. 550 BC.

q.q: The Maya civilization was at its peak from about:
q.explanation: The Maya civilization was at its peak from about 250-900 AD.

q.q: The Maya developed an accurate yearly calendar.
q.explanation: The Maya made outstanding achievements in astronomy and mathematics and developed an accurate yearly calendar.

q.q: What was the capital of the Inca Empire?
q.answer: Cusco|Cuzco
q.explanation: Its capital was Cusco, in southern Peru.

q.q: The Inca Empire began to expand at about:
q.explanation: The Inca Empire began to expand at about 1438.

q.q: The Aztec capital, which stood on the site of present-day Mexico City, was:
q.explanation: The largest city was the capital Tenochtitlan, on the site of present-day Mexico City.

q.q: Name the form of writing used by the Aztecs.
q.answer: pictographic writing|pictographic
q.explanation: They used a form of writing called pictographic writing.

q.q: The Inca built a network of roads and were skilled in engineering.
q.explanation: The Inca were skilled in engineering and crafts and built a network of roads.

q.q: The Aztec empire was destroyed by the Spaniards in:
q.explanation: The Aztec empire was destroyed by the Spaniards in 1521.

q.q: Explain what the Maya built for worship and where the temples were placed.
q.answer: tall limestone pyramids with small temples on top|limestone pyramids
q.explanation: The Maya built tall pyramids of limestone with small temples on top.

q.q: What craft material did Inca craftworkers use besides cotton and wool?
q.answer: gold|silver
q.explanation: Inca craftworkers made fine artifacts from gold, silver and other materials.

q.q: Arrange these events from earliest to latest.
options: The Spaniards destroy the Aztec empire
The Maya civilization is at its peak
The Inca Empire begins to expand
Spanish forces conquer the Inca Empire
q.explanation: Order: Maya peak 250-900 AD, Inca expansion c. 1438, Aztec fall 1521, Inca conquest after 1532.

q.q: The smaller political unit in which Greek culture developed was the:
q.explanation: Greek culture developed chiefly in small city-states called polis.

q.q: The two best-known Greek city-states were:
q.explanation: The best-known city-states were Athens and Sparta.

q.q: The Greek city-states were united into a single nation.
q.explanation: The city-states never became united into a nation, though they shared language, religion and culture.

q.q: Who was the Greek physician who began the tradition of modern medicine in Europe?
q.answer: Hippocrates
q.explanation: Hippocrates began the tradition of modern medicine in Europe.

q.q: The Roman Republic was established in:
q.explanation: The Roman Republic was established in 509 BC after the Roman nobles overthrew the king.

q.q: In the Roman Republic, who served for only one year?
q.explanation: Two elected consuls headed the government, and a consul served for only a year, while senators served for life.

q.q: Give the name of the temple of Athena in Athens, the finest example of Greek architecture.
q.answer: the Parthenon|Parthenon
q.explanation: The temple of Athena in Athens, the Parthenon, is the finest example of Greek architecture.

q.q: The Roman Republic lasted nearly 500 years, until 27 BC.
q.explanation: The Roman Republic lasted nearly 500 years, until 27 BC, when the Empire was established.

q.q: Explain the main difference between the Roman Republic and the Roman Empire.
q.answer: the Republic was democratic and the Empire was run by one man|rule by one man
q.explanation: The former was a democratic society and the latter was run only by one man.

q.q: Against which city did Rome fight the Punic wars (264-146 BC)?
q.answer: Carthage
q.explanation: The bloodiest wars of Rome were the repetitive Punic wars fought against Carthage.

q.q: Arrange these Roman and Greek events in correct chronological order.
q.explanation: Order: Rome founded c. 753 BC, Republic 509 BC, Empire 27 BC, Rome falls 476 AD.

q.q: Christianity began in Palestine in the:
q.explanation: Christianity began in Palestine in the first century AD.

q.q: In which town was Jesus born?
q.answer: Bethlehem
q.explanation: Jesus was born in Bethlehem, in the Judea part of Palestine.

q.q: The Roman government began persecuting Christians during the reign of Nero (AD 54-68).
q.explanation: The Roman government began persecuting Christians during the reign of Nero (AD 54-68).

q.q: The Edict of Milan, which ordered religious toleration, was issued in:
q.explanation: Constantine ordered religious toleration in the Edict of Milan in 313 AD.

q.q: Give the term for the belief in one God.
q.answer: monotheism
q.explanation: Monotheism is the belief in one God.

q.q: Under which ruler did the Romans adopt Christianity as their official religion in 392 AD?
q.explanation: Under Theodosius the Great, who ruled from 378 to 395, the Romans adopted Christianity as their official religion in 392 AD.

q.q: In 1054 the Christian Church split into two parts. These were:
q.explanation: In 1054 the Church split into the Roman Catholic Church at Rome and the Eastern Orthodox Church at Constantinople.

q.q: The Edict of Milan made Christianity the official religion of the Roman Empire.
q.explanation: The Edict of Milan granted religious toleration; Christianity became the official religion only in 392 AD under Theodosius.

q.q: Explain why the Roman government persecuted Christians.
q.answer: they were seen as a threat to the unity of the Empire|a threat to the unity of the Empire
q.explanation: The Roman governments considered the Christians a threat against the unity of the Empire.

q.q: What event in 1517 divided Western Christianity into the Roman Catholic Church and Protestantism?
q.answer: the Reformation|Reformation movement
q.explanation: In 1517 a Reformation movement began, dividing Western Christianity into the Roman Catholic Church and Protestantism.

q.q: Arrange these events in correct chronological order.
options: Christianity becomes the official religion in 392 AD
q.explanation: Order: persecution under Nero (AD 54-68), Edict of Milan (313 AD), official religion (392 AD), the split of 1054.

q.q: How many major language super-families do linguists identify in Ethiopia and the Horn?
q.explanation: The two super-families are Afro-Asiatic and Nilo-Saharan.

q.q: Which language family is spoken by the largest number of people in Ethiopia and the Horn?
q.explanation: Cushitic speakers form the vast majority in both area and numbers.

q.q: The Beja language represents which branch of Cushitic?
q.explanation: North Cushitic is represented only by the Beja people's language.

q.q: Agaw languages such as Qimant and Awign belong to:
q.explanation: Central Cushitic is represented by Bilen and the Agaw languages.

q.q: Gafat is an example of an Ethiopian language that has disappeared.
q.explanation: Gafat, a Southern Semitic language, is now extinct.

q.q: The Nilo-Saharan super-family in Ethiopia is divided into Chari-Nile and Koman.
q.explanation: These are the two families of the Nilo-Saharan super-family.

q.q: Name the two major language super-families of Ethiopia and the Horn.
q.answer: afro-asiatic and nilo-saharan|afroasiatic and nilo-saharan
q.explanation: They are Afro-Asiatic and Nilo-Saharan.

q.q: Give the term for the mixing of religious beliefs and practices, such as indigenous customs fused with Christianity or Islam.
q.answer: syncretism
q.explanation: This mixing is known as syncretism.

q.q: Christianity became the state religion of Aksum after Frumentius converted:
q.explanation: Frumentius converted King Ezana (r. 320-350 AD).

q.q: In which year AD did the first group of Muslim refugees arrive at Aksum?
q.explanation: The refugees arrived in 615 AD.

q.q: Arrange these events in the correct chronological order.
options: The first Muslim refugees arrive at Aksum
The Nine Saints arrive in Ethiopia
q.explanation: The order is: Frumentius converts Ezana about 330, the Nine Saints arrive at the end of the fifth century, refugees arrive in 615, Adulis is destroyed in 702.

q.q: Which state had trade relations with Egypt since the third millennium BC?
q.explanation: Egyptian records place Punt south of Egypt with trade since the third millennium BC.

q.q: Historians place the territory of Punt in the coastal parts of present-day:
q.explanation: Punt lay along the Red Sea and Indian Ocean coasts of these present-day countries.

q.q: Which of the following was an export of Punt to Egypt?
q.explanation: Ostrich feathers were exported by Punt; hatchets, daggers and necklaces were sent by Egypt.

q.q: Yeha is located about 30 kilometres north-east of Aksum.
q.explanation: The textbook places Yeha 30 km north-east of Aksum.

q.q: Between which two years BC did the wealth of Yeha reach its peak?
q.explanation: Yeha's wealth peaked between 750 and 500 BC.

q.q: Damat's rulers adopted which South Arabian political and religious title?
q.explanation: The rulers of Damat adopted the South Arabian title Mukarib.

q.q: Which Red Sea port did Damat use for its trade?
q.answer: adulis
q.explanation: Damat used the Red Sea coast port of Adulis.

q.q: Why do historians no longer believe that Aksum was the first centralised polity in Ethiopia and the Horn?
options: States such as Punt, Yeha and Damat existed before Aksum
q.explanation: Several principalities emerged and declined before the rise of Aksum.

q.q: The other pre-Aksumite states named in the lesson emerged from about 1000 BC.
q.explanation: These states emerged from about 1000 BC.

q.q: Arrange these centres from earliest to latest.
q.explanation: The order is: Punt (third millennium BC), Yeha (about 1000 BC), Damat, then Aksum (first century AD).

q.q: Aksum emerged in the first century AD with its nucleus at:
q.explanation: The city of Aksum was the political and religious centre of the kingdom.

q.q: Which port was the main outlet for Aksumite external trade?
q.explanation: Aksum generated income from trade through the port of Adulis.

q.q: Aksumite kings minted coins of:
q.explanation: Coins of bronze, silver and gold were minted to facilitate trade.

q.q: Which sequence correctly explains the decline of Aksum?
options: Loss of the Red Sea trade after Adulis fell in 702 AD, then internal rebellion and Beja pressure
Defeat by the Zagwe in 1150 AD
Conquest by Portugal in the sixteenth century
The founding of Ifat in 896 AD
q.explanation: The decline began with the loss of the Red Sea trade and was worsened by rebellion and Beja attacks.

q.q: Between the fourth and sixth centuries Aksum expanded beyond the Red Sea into southern Arabia.
q.explanation: Aksumite kings expanded east beyond the Red Sea into southern Arabia.

q.q: Who was the last Aksumite king deposed by the Zagwe around 1150 AD?
q.answer: dil naod
q.explanation: Dil Naod was the last Aksumite king, deposed around 1150 AD.

q.q: Name the language that served as the lingua franca of the Red Sea and the Mediterranean before Geez spread in Aksum.
q.answer: greek
q.explanation: Greek was the lingua franca of the Red Sea and Mediterranean region at that time.

q.q: King Kaleb controlled South Arabia in:
q.explanation: Kaleb controlled South Arabia in 525 AD.

q.q: Aksum lost control of the trade on the other side of the Red Sea after the South Arabians expelled its governors between 580 and 590 AD.
q.explanation: The expulsion ended Aksumite control of South Arabia.

q.q: By the late ninth century the Aksumite state had taken refuge in an area inhabited mainly by:
q.explanation: After being pushed to Kubar, the state took refuge among the Agaw people.

q.q: The Zagwe dynasty was founded around 1150 AD by:
q.explanation: Mera Tekle Haymnot founded the dynasty around 1150 AD.

q.q: The capital of the Zagwe dynasty was at:
q.explanation: Mera Tekle Haymnot established a new capital at Adefa (Roha) in Lasta.

q.q: The Zagwe dynasty is best known in Ethiopian history for its:
q.explanation: Zagwe is remembered for the rock-hewn churches at Roha.

q.q: How many rock-hewn churches were built during the reign of Emperor Lalibela?
q.explanation: Eleven rock-hewn churches survive from the reign of Emperor Lalibela.

q.q: The rise of the Zagwe was a shift of power to the Cushitic-speaking Agaw rather than the creation of a new kingdom.
q.explanation: The founding of Zagwe was a political power shift, not a new kingdom.

q.q: Which Amhara chief defeated the last Zagwe king in 1270 AD?
q.answer: yekuno amlak
q.explanation: Yekuno Amlak organised the movement and defeated the last Zagwe king.

q.q: Name the last Zagwe king defeated in 1270 AD.
q.answer: yetbarek
q.explanation: Yetbarek was the last Zagwe king.

q.q: Which two regions provided the strongest opposition to Zagwe rule?
q.answer: tigray and amhara
q.explanation: Strong opposition came from Tigray and Amhara.

q.q: What was the main economic base of the Zagwe dynasty?
options: Sea trade in the Red Sea only
Agriculture, with trade bringing additional income
q.explanation: The economy was based on agriculture, with trade adding income.

q.q: Which port was the main outlet during the Zagwe period?
q.explanation: The Zeila port was the main outlet during Zagwe times.

q.q: Yekuno Amlak claimed descent from Dil Naod and restored the so-called Solomonic dynasty.
q.explanation: His genealogy linked him to the last Aksumite king, Dil Naod.

q.q: Which Muslim sultanate was established first in the region?
q.explanation: The sultanate of Shewa was the first to be established.

q.q: The sultanate of Shewa was founded in:
q.explanation: The sultanate of Shewa was established in 896 AD.

q.q: Because its founders claimed descent from a clan of southern Arabia, the ruling dynasty of Shewa was known as the:
q.explanation: Its founders claimed descent from the Makhzunmite clan, so the dynasty was called Makhzunmite.

q.q: The sultanate of Shewa was located in the hot lowland region on the left of the Awash River.
q.explanation: The textbook places Shewa on the left of the Awash in the hot lowlands.

q.q: Which port became the most crucial gateway for Islam into the Horn of Africa?
q.explanation: Zeila became the most crucial gateway for Islam into the Horn.

q.q: Who founded the Walasma dynasty of Ifat in 1285 AD?
q.answer: umar walasma
q.explanation: Umar Walasma founded Ifat in 1285 AD.

q.q: What was the main source of conflict between Ifat and the Christian highland state after 1270?
q.answer: control of the zeila trade|the zeila trade|trade routes
q.explanation: The need to control the Zeila trade became the main source of conflict.

q.q: An internal power struggle within the ruling family contributed to the final decline of Shewa.
q.explanation: The ruling family's internal struggle later led to the state's final decline.

q.q: The main reason northern Ethiopian trade declined was:
options: Arab control of the Red Sea and the destruction of Adulis
the fall of Shewa in 896 AD
q.explanation: Arab control of the Red Sea and the destruction of Adulis reduced northern trade.

q.q: Which state became the strongest Muslim sultanate and the main rival of the Christian highland kingdom?
q.explanation: Ifat became the strongest Muslim sultanate and the strongest rival of the Christian highland state.

q.q: The Dark Age in Western Europe is dated:
q.explanation: The Dark Age was a period of West European history from 500 AD to 1000 AD.

q.q: In feudalism, a fief was:
q.explanation: A fief, or feud, is a piece of land given by a higher lord to a lower lord.

q.q: The basic units of European feudalism were manors, or villages.
q.explanation: The basic units of European feudalism were manors, or villages, and the manorial lord held power over the peasants.

q.q: The Byzantine Empire was the:
q.explanation: The Byzantine Empire was the East Roman Empire which continued after the fall of the West Roman Empire.

q.q: In which year was the Battle of Manzikert fought?
q.explanation: Byzantium suffered a disastrous defeat at the Battle of Manzikert in 1071.

q.q: Give the name of the system in which a higher lord gave land to a lower lord who then owed service.
q.answer: vassalage|feudalism
q.explanation: This is the vassalage system, the core of feudalism.

q.q: The Orthodox Church officially separated from the Roman Catholic Church in:
q.explanation: The Orthodox Church was officially separated from the Roman Catholic Church in 1054.

q.q: West European feudal society gave peasants, craftsmen and traders real political power.
q.explanation: The mass of feudal society had no political and economic power and was exploited.

q.q: Explain one merit and one demerit of the medieval period.
q.answer: merit: stability and church schools and castles|demerit: exploitation war and blood feuds
q.explanation: The period produced churches, castles and record keeping, but also war, murder, blood feuds and the exploitation of peasants.

q.q: The Crusades began in the 1090s mainly in order to:
options: liberate the Christian holy lands from the Seljuk Turks
q.explanation: The crusades were wars of Christian Europe against the Seljuk Turks to liberate Christian holy lands.

q.q: Which emperor brought the Byzantine Empire to the height of its territory and power?
q.answer: Justinian
q.explanation: The Byzantine Empire was at its height under Emperor Justinian (r. 527-565).

q.q: Islam began in the Arabian Peninsula with the teaching of the Prophet Mohammed in Mecca around:
q.explanation: Islam began around 610 AD with the Prophet's life and teaching in Mecca.

q.q: What is the name of the journey from Mecca to Medina in 622 AD?
q.answer: Hejira|Hijra
q.explanation: The journey is called the Hejira, and it began the Islamic calendar.

q.q: The term Islam means submission to the will of Allah (God).
q.explanation: Islam means submission to the will of Allah, and worshippers are called Muslims.

q.q: In 1453 the Ottoman Turks captured:
q.explanation: The Ottomans conquered Constantinople in 1453 and renamed it Istanbul.

q.q: The highly trained soldiers of the Ottoman Empire were called:
q.explanation: The Ottomans formed a group of highly trained soldiers called janissaries.

q.q: Give the term for the authority and legitimacy to rule China, which a corrupt dynasty was believed to lose.
q.answer: mandate of Heaven
q.explanation: A corrupt and weak dynasty lost the mandate of Heaven and was replaced.

q.q: Arrange the four groups of Ottoman society from highest to lowest rank.
q.explanation: The order is Sultan, grand viziers, janissaries, occupational groups.

q.q: Turkish expansion in Europe was ended in 1571 by the:
q.explanation: European fleets defeated the Turkish navy at the Battle of Lepanto near Greece in 1571.

q.q: The Ottomans banned European merchants from going to the Far East.
q.explanation: The Ottomans controlled the trade route from Europe to Asia and banned European merchants from the Far East.

q.q: Explain how a dynasty lost the mandate of Heaven in the Chinese dynastic cycle.
q.answer: it became corrupt and weak and lost the support of the people|corruption and weak rule cost it legitimacy
q.explanation: When a dynasty ruled well it kept the mandate; when it became corrupt, weak and unsupported it lost it and was replaced.

q.q: After the death of the Prophet, under which two dynasties did Muslims come?
q.answer: Umayyad and Abbasid
q.explanation: Muslims came under the Arab Caliphates of the Umayyad and then the Abbasid dynasties.

q.q: What distinguished capitalism from previous systems?
options: Spending wealth on pyramids and cathedrals
Using accumulated capital to enlarge productive capacity
q.explanation: Capitalism used accumulated capital to enlarge productive capacity rather than invest in unproductive enterprises.

q.q: Old Roman cities were restored and became centres of production and exchange.
q.explanation: Trade revived slowly and old Roman cities were restored as centres of production and exchange.

q.q: Which of the following was a problem for long-distance trade?
q.explanation: Heavy tolls, transport difficulties and insecurity from war and robbery were the chief trade problems.

q.q: Give the term for heavy taxes charged on the transit of commodities.
q.answer: tolls
q.explanation: Heavy tolls were taxes charged on the transit of commodities.

q.q: City-states were the political, economic and social life centres of:
q.explanation: City-states were the political, economic and social life centres in Renaissance Italy.

q.q: Explain what merchants learned to do in the revived towns.
q.answer: buy raw materials have workers manufacture and sell finished products at the best prices|organise production and exchange
q.explanation: Merchants bought raw materials, had workers manufacture goods and sold the finished products at the best prices.

q.q: The Crusades contributed to the revival of trade in the Middle Ages.
q.explanation: The crusades contributed to the revival of trade in the Middle Ages.

q.q: Explain how the discoveries and colonial conquest promoted capitalism.
q.answer: profits from trade and colonies were reinvested|big profits promoted faster development of capitalism
q.explanation: After the discoveries big profits were made, and colonial conquest helped promote the faster development of capitalism.

q.q: Which statement best describes capital in early capitalism?
options: Accumulated wealth invested in production and trade
A tax paid to a lord
q.explanation: Capital is accumulated wealth that early capitalists invested to enlarge productive capacity.

q.q: In which country did city-states become centres of economic and political life?
q.answer: Italy
q.explanation: City-states were the life centres in Renaissance Italy.

q.q: The age of European explorations and discoveries took place in the:
q.explanation: The age of European explorations and discoveries was in the fifteenth and sixteenth centuries.

q.q: Which explorer discovered a new sea route to India in 1498?
q.answer: Vasco da Gama|Vasco da Gama
q.explanation: The Portuguese explorer Vasco da Gama reached India by a new sea route in 1498.

q.q: Which of the following explorers reached America in 1492?
q.explanation: Christopher Columbus was the first European explorer to reach America in 1492.

q.q: America was named after the Italian mapmaker Amerigo Vespucci.
q.explanation: The land came to be known as America from the name of the Italian mapmaker Amerigo Vespucci.

q.q: Explain the main reason why Europeans wanted to bypass the old trade route to the Far East.
q.answer: the Ottoman Turkish blockade of the trade route|Ottoman control and tolls on the route
q.explanation: The explorations were partly initiated by the need to bypass the Ottoman Turkish blockade of the old long-distance trade route.

q.q: Arrange these events in correct chronological order, earliest first.
q.explanation: The Ottoman conquest was 1453, Columbus 1492, Vasco da Gama 1498 and Magellan 1519-1522.

q.q: Who circumnavigated the world between 1519 and 1522?
q.explanation: The Portuguese Ferdinand Magellan circumnavigated the world between 1519 and 1522 in the service of Spain.

q.q: Name the two leading European nations in exploration and discoveries in the 15th and 16th centuries.
q.answer: Spain and Portugal|Portugal and Spain
q.explanation: Spain and Portugal were the leaders, closely followed by Holland, Britain, France and Russia.

q.q: The discoveries reduced the development of capitalism in Europe.
q.explanation: The voyages, with colonial conquest, promoted the faster development of capitalism.

q.q: Which invention mentioned in the lesson helped sailors on long voyages?
q.explanation: New inventions such as the compass aided European long-distance exploration.

q.q: Explain one economic impact of the discoveries on Europe.
q.answer: huge profits from local trade networks|faster development of capitalism|growth of globalisation
q.explanation: Europeans gained huge profits from trade networks, which enhanced globalisation and, with colonial conquest, promoted capitalism.

q.q: The word Renaissance means:
q.explanation: The word renaissance indicates the rebirth of learning.

q.q: The Renaissance began in Italy and spread to the rest of Europe.
q.explanation: The Renaissance began in Italy and spread mainly to England, France, Germany, Spain and Holland.

q.q: Who painted the Last Supper and the Monalisa?
q.explanation: The Italian Leonardo da Vinci painted the Last Supper and the Monalisa.

q.q: Which Polish thinker declared that the earth revolved around the sun?
q.answer: Nicholas Copernicus|Copernicus
q.explanation: The Polish Nicholas Copernicus declared that the earth revolved around the sun.

q.q: Give the term for the national language used in Renaissance writing instead of Latin.
q.answer: vernacular
q.explanation: Renaissance writers used the vernacular, such as Italian and English, rather than Latin.

q.q: Which of these was written by the Englishman Thomas More?
q.explanation: Utopia was written by the Englishman Thomas More.

q.q: The Renaissance began in the 14th century and ended in the 17th century.
q.explanation: It began in the 14th century and ended in the 17th century.

q.q: Explain the new view of human beings that emerged in Renaissance Italy.
q.answer: emphasis on individual ability|people emphasised individual ability and human potential
q.explanation: A new view of human beings emerged as people emphasised individual ability.

q.q: Which Renaissance figure studied human anatomy?
q.explanation: The Belgian Vesalius studied human anatomy.

q.q: Arrange the three features of Renaissance Italy in the order given in the lesson.
options: An age of recovery from the disasters of the fourteenth century
A new view of human beings emphasising individual ability
q.explanation: First it was an urban society; second an age of recovery; third a new view of human beings.

q.q: Explain how the Renaissance influenced the modern world.
q.answer: new focus on humanism|recognition of human potential and scientific inquiry|turning away from church-dominated ideas
q.explanation: The Renaissance brought a new focus on humanism and recognition of human potential and scientific inquiry, which still influence societies today.

q.q: The Reformation began in Germany, led by:
q.explanation: It began in Germany led by Martin Luther in 1517.

q.q: The Calvinist followers in France were called Huguenots.
q.explanation: The Calvinist followers in French were called Huguenots.

q.q: In Britain, the Protestant national church established during the Reformation was known as:
q.explanation: The English Protestants established a national church called the Anglican Church.

q.q: In which year did Martin Luther begin the Reformation?
q.explanation: The Reformation began in Germany led by Martin Luther in 1517.

q.q: The Society of Jesus was founded in Spain in 1534 by:
q.explanation: The Society of Jesus was formed in Spain by Ignatius Loyola in 1534.

q.q: Give the name of the Catholic reform movement carried out in response to the Protestant challenge.
q.answer: Counter-Reformation|Catholic Counter-Reformation
q.explanation: The Catholic Church carried out the Counter-Reformation to reform itself in response to Protestantism.

q.q: John Knox founded the Anglican Church in England.
q.explanation: John Knox founded Presbyterianism in Scotland; the Anglican Church came from Henry VIII and Elizabeth I in England.

q.q: Which 1648 peace ended the Thirty Years' War in Germany?
q.answer: Peace of Westphalia
q.explanation: The Peace of Westphalia ended the war in Germany in 1648.

q.q: Explain the four kinds of causes of the Reformation.
q.answer: social political religious and economic causes
q.explanation: The causes of the Reformation were social, political, religious and economic.

q.q: The Thirty Years' War lasted from:
q.explanation: The Reformation played an essential role in the Thirty Years' War, which lasted from 1618 to 1648.

q.q: Arrange these events in the correct order, earliest first.
options: The Society of Jesus is founded
q.explanation: The order is 1517 Luther, 1534 Society of Jesus, 1560 Knox, 1648 Peace of Westphalia.

q.q: The Industrial Revolution means the invention and use of machines in place of:
q.explanation: The term means the invention and use of machines in place of hard labour.

q.q: The Industrial Revolution began in:
q.explanation: It began in Great Britain in the 1780s and spread over several decades.

q.q: Steam power replaced the early wind and water power.
q.explanation: The new steam power replaced the early wind and water power.

q.q: Who improved the steam engines between 1782 and 1784?
q.answer: James Watt|Watt
